memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As morning dawned, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys." — Gen 44:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is a beautiful morning. The sun is up, the donkeys are loaded, the sacks are full, and the brothers are heading home with Benjamin safe beside them. Everything looks settled. Everything looks finished.

But it is not. Something is hidden in one of those sacks that will change the whole day.

How often life feels exactly like this. We think we have come through the hard part. We breathe out. We start planning the future. And then something we did not see coming turns the day upside down. Joseph's brothers rode out of the city thinking their troubles were behind them, not knowing they were riding straight into the hardest moment of their lives.

Here is the comfort: what looked like disaster was, in God's hands, the doorway to reconciliation. The interruption on the road was the mercy that finally brought this broken family back together. The brothers could not have arranged it. They would never have chosen it. But they needed it.

We do not always know what God is doing when a settled morning turns into a difficult day. What we do know is His character. He is a Father who works all things together for the good of those who love Him (Rom 8:28) — not always for our comfort, but always for our good.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When has an unexpected interruption turned out to be something God used for good?
2. How do you usually react when a peaceful day suddenly turns difficult?
3. What would change if you trusted God's goodness in the middle of an interruption, not just afterwards?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not always understand the turns my days take. Help me to trust that You are good even when the road becomes difficult, and to remember that You are always working. Amen.
